'''Carrie Ichikawa Jenkins''' is a Canadian philosopher who holds a [[Canada Research Chair]]<ref name=autogenerated1>{{cite web|url=http://www.chairs-chaires.gc.ca/chairholders-titulaires/profile-eng.aspx?profileId=2870|title=Canada Research Chair – Profile|work=chairs-chaires.gc.ca|date=2012-11-29}}</ref> and is Professor of Philosophy at the [[University of British Columbia]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://philosophy.ubc.ca/persons/carrie-jenkins/|title=Carrie Jenkins – Department of Philosophy|work=ubc.ca}}</ref> She is also a professor at the Northern Institute of Philosophy, [[University of Aberdeen]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.abdn.ac.uk/nip/page?id=73|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20140326183100/http://www.abdn.ac.uk/nip/page?id=73|url-status=dead|title=Northern Institute of Philosophy|archivedate=March 26, 2014}}</ref> Her primary research areas are [[epistemology]], [[metaphysics]], [[philosophy of logic]], [[philosophy of language]], and [[philosophy of mathematics]].<ref name=autogenerated2>{{Cite web |url=http://dl.dropboxusercontent.com/u/2480139/CV.pdf |title=Archived copy |access-date=2014-04-21 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161108004231/https://dl.dropboxusercontent.com/u/2480139/CV.pdf |archive-date=2016-11-08 |url-status=dead }}</ref> She is one of the principal editors of the journal ''[[Thought: A Journal of Philosophy|Thought]]''.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/journal/10.1002/(ISSN)2161-2234|title=Thought: A Journal of Philosophy |publisher=Wiley |doi=10.1002/(ISSN)2161-2234}}</ref>

==Education and career==
Jenkins holds BA, MPhil and PhD degrees in philosophy from [[Trinity College, Cambridge]].<ref name=autogenerated2 />

She has held teaching and research positions at the [[University of St Andrews]], the [[Australian National University]], the [[University of Michigan]] and the [[University of Nottingham]].<ref name=autogenerated2 /> She was head of the department of philosophy at the University of Nottingham from 2010 to 2011.<ref name=autogenerated2 />

Jenkins was awarded a [[Canada Research Chair]] by the Canadian Government in 2011.<ref name=autogenerated1 />

Jenkins is also a member of the philosophy-themed musical group The 21st Century Monads.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://the21stcenturymonads.net/|title=The 21st Century Monads|work=the21stcenturymonads.net}}</ref>

Jenkins has advocated for a more holistic view of academic life, blending creative writing, public engagement, and even tarot readings into her philosophical practice. She refers to this interdisciplinary integration as a form of "life crafting" and "love crafting," emphasizing flexibility and resistance to institutional constraints.<ref>{{cite web |title=Romance, Reason, Rebellion: Carrie Jenkins on Redefining Love |url=https://tarotinterviews.com/episode/romance-reason-rebellion-carrie-jenkins-on-redefining-love |website=Tarot Interviews |date=2025-04-15 |access-date=2025-05-16}}</ref>

Jenkins became involved in a dispute with [[Brian Leiter]], a professor at the [[University of Chicago]] and then editor of the [[Philosophical Gourmet Report]]. His emailed remarks about Jenkins led to hundreds of philosophers refusing to provide data for the report, and ultimately led to his stepping down as its editor.<ref name=chron1>{{cite journal|last1=Schmidt|first1=Peter|title=The Man Who Ranks Philosophy Departments Now Rankles Them, Too|url=http://chronicle.com/article/The-Man-Who-Ranks-Philosophy/149007/|journal=The Chronicle of Higher Education|access-date=September 30, 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140926193400/http://chronicle.com/article/The-Man-Who-Ranks-Philosophy/149007/|archive-date=September 26, 2014|url-status=live|date=September 26, 2014}}</ref><ref name="chronicle.com1">{{cite web|url=http://chronicle.com/blogs/ticker/controversial-philosopher-will-step-down-as-editor-of-influential-rankings/87797|title=Controversial Philosopher Will Step Down as Editor of Influential Rankings|work=[[The Chronicle of Higher Education]] |date=October 10, 2014|author=Andy Thomason}}</ref>

==Personal life==
As of 2017, Jenkins has both a boyfriend and a husband. That year she stated, "I've been openly nonmonogamous for five or six years. Over the last four years, I’ve been involved in several long-term simultaneous relationships, and so the term [[polyamory]] has felt more appropriate."<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.vox.com/conversations/2017/2/23/14684236/monogamy-valentines-day-polyamory-marriage-love|title=A philosopher makes the case for polyamory|first=Sean|last=Illing|date=February 23, 2017|website=Vox}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Weigel |first=Moira |date=2017-02-03 |title=‘I Have Multiple Loves’ |url=https://www.chronicle.com/article/i-have-multiple-loves/ |access-date=2026-07-06 |website=The Chronicle of Higher Education |language=en}}</ref>
